research.title: AEGIS-Test: Adaptive Evidence-Guided Iterative Synthesis for Reliable LLM-Based Software Testing
research.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) can rapidly draft software tests, their output frequently suffers from hallucinated assertions, unexecutable test harnesses, and semantic coverage gaps. AEGIS-Test introduces an adaptive, evidence-guided iterative synthesis framework that pairs LLM code generation with deterministic execution feedback, AST static validation, and dynamic mutation testing. Experimental results show a 42% reduction in non-compiling test cases and significant branch-coverage improvement over raw LLM zero-shot prompts.
objectives: Mitigate LLM hallucination in automated test suite generation.
Construct an automated feedback loop combining Python AST analysis and runtime execution logs.
Benchmark branch coverage and mutation score against industry baselines.
research.methodology: Iterative prompt synthesis guided by execution trace analysis, semantic mutation scoring, and assertion boundary checking.

research.title: A Computational Perspective on Breast Cancer Detection in Ultrasound: Fusion of Multi-Image Modalities
research.abstract: Ultrasound imaging is an essential diagnostic tool in oncology, but standard B-mode sonography frequently suffers from speckle noise, low contrast, and operator dependency. This research presents a computational approach fusing multi-image ultrasound modalities (B-mode and Doppler) through deep convolutional feature extraction. Evaluated across benchmark sonographic datasets, the fused pipeline demonstrates substantial gains in diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, and AUC-ROC, providing a dependable computational aid for early oncological screening.
objectives: Investigate computational limitations of single-modality B-mode ultrasound.
Engineer a multi-image feature fusion architecture combining acoustic reflectance and vascular Doppler signals.
Demonstrate measurable diagnostic accuracy improvements over standard single-image baselines.
research.methodology: Pre-processing via adaptive speckle filtering, dual-stream convolutional neural feature extraction, cross-attention feature fusion layer, and binary lesion classification with Bayesian uncertainty estimation.
